title: Fitting a wet wall shower panel to a stud wall
subtitle: Adhesive-fix waterproof acrylic or PVC shower wall panels to a plasterboard stud wall
excerpt: How to fit wet-wall shower panels to a timber stud wall lined with moisture-resistant plasterboard. Covers scribing the panels to the wall, cutting, applying panel adhesive, and sealing the joints and base trim.
sourceNotes: Collins Complete DIY Manual (referenced, not reproduced). UK bathroom fitting trade practice.

glossaryTerms.definition: A rigid acrylic, PVC, or foam-core sheet, 2400 x 900 mm or 1000 mm wide and 4 to 11 mm thick, used to line shower enclosures and wet room walls. Panels are waterproof and require no grout. They are adhesive-fixed to a solid substrate and sealed at the joints and base with silicone.

A plasterboard with a green-coloured facing paper and a treated gypsum core that resists short-term dampness. Standard abbreviation: MR board or green board. It is the minimum substrate behind wet-wall panels on a stud wall; standard grey plasterboard will delaminate in a wet area.

and seal at the joints and base with silicone. The result is watertight, grout-free, and straightforward to fit over a weekend.

The substrate must be flat, rigid, and dry. On a timber stud wall, fix 12.5 mm MR plasterboard directly to the studs with drywall screws at 300 mm centres and tape and joint the seams. Allow any fresh plaster or compound to dry fully before panelling. Existing tiled walls are often a suitable substrate; check they are fully bonded before fitting panels over the top.
Plan the layout and cut the panels

Measure the height from the shower tray or bath rim to the ceiling. Most wet-wall panels are 2400 mm tall; if the ceiling is higher, panels need topping or adding a border. Scribe each panel to the wall using a spirit level and pencil. Cut panels face-down with a jigsaw to avoid chipping the decorative surface, or score-and-snap with a utility knife and straight-edge. Allow a 3 mm gap at the base for the silicone seal and a 2 mm gap between panels for the corner trims.
Apply the adhesive and fit the panels

Apply panel adhesive (use a solvent-free adhesive specified for wet-wall panels; most manufacturers supply their own product) in vertical beads 150 mm apart across the back of the panel, and a continuous bead around the perimeter 25 mm in from the edge. Position the panel on the wall, press firmly over each bead, and prop in place with temporary packers at the base. Use the spirit level to check plumb before the adhesive skins. Leave undisturbed for the adhesive open time stated by the manufacturer (usually 24 to 48 hours).

Fit internal corner trims, external corner trims, and start/end trims by pressing them over the panel edge. Most trims clip or friction-fit; some require a bead of adhesive behind the trim flange. Once all trims are in place, run a continuous bead of neutral-cure silicone along the base of each panel where it meets the shower tray or bath rim, along every internal corner joint, and along any wall-to-panel edge. Smooth the silicone with a damp finger, and allow 24 hours before the shower is used.

attrs.symptom: Panels bow away from the wall between adhesive beads
attrs.cause: Adhesive bead spacing too wide or substrate not flat.
attrs.fix: Apply more adhesive beads or use temporary battens screwed through the panel face at stud positions to hold the panel flat until the adhesive cures. Fill screw holes with matching caulk.

attrs.symptom: Silicone joint fails and water penetrates at the base
attrs.cause: Silicone applied before the adhesive fully cured, or the tray rim flexes under load.
attrs.fix: Cut out the failed silicone bead with a utility knife and re-seal with a fresh bead of sanitary-grade silicone. Clean the surfaces with isopropyl alcohol before re-sealing.
